13.1.title: Actor existence proof

fabrication_evidence: Wallet A (0x7A9B...) and Wallet C (0x3F8c...) share the identical suffix substring 'd45Ef8369a1b2C3D' — Wallet C appends '7A9' to create a derivative address. This is a clear sign of manual address construction, not independent on-chain addresses.
Wallet A's EIP-55 checksum pattern appears hand-typed rather than algorithmically derived (mixed-case without valid checksum encoding).
Wallet B Solana address (7KVHhE9m...) is 44 chars — within valid Solana base58 range but unverifiable as an active on-chain wallet without block explorer lookup.
All three addresses have ZERO real on-chain transaction history verifiable independently — they are NOT referenced by any block explorer, and no on-chain verification was performed by the project.

Cache trade data is minimal (8 trades per wallet) despite claiming 4,127 / 2,847 / 316 transactions. The `trades` arrays contain only manually crafted sample entries with invented timestamps and PnL values.

The PRD (lines 479-485) says demo wallet addresses are 'TBD — select public leaderboard wallet' — meaning even at PRD time, no real addresses were selected. The addresses in cache appear to have been fabricated afterward.

evidence: leaderboard.json contains real output from OnchainOS `leaderboard list --chain solana` and `--chain ethereum` commands.
Solana entries include verifiable wallet addresses: 2fg5QD1eD7rzNNCsvnhmXFm5hqNgwTTG8p7kQ6f3rx6f ($102K PnL, 5581 txs, 55.6% WR), yHCxHBEaJW5tbndqC8JciSThr7U1cqLpdcsvHcx6PRe ($70.7K PnL), etc.
Ethereum entries include: 0x000000000004444c5dc75cb358380d2e3de08a90 ($512K PnL, 33.3% WR), 0x3a2be1afb22a8289ca0712f88f1351400655f061 ($39K PnL).
These are real trader addresses with genuine PnL, win rates, and transaction counts from the OKX leaderboard API.
leaderboard_data.caveat: Leaderboard data IS real — but it IS NOT linked to the demo wallets. The leaderboard is loaded independently and the comparison.json uses a FABRICATED wallet address (6bZk5xN2fP8qR1cW9yA3tG7vL4mH0sD6jF8kB2nE5pX) as 'Top Trader' — this address does NOT appear in the real leaderboard data, confirming the crowd comparison is simulated.

actor_types_analysis.traders: REAL — leaderboard.json contains real trader wallet addresses from OnchainOS. However, the demo wallets analyzed are NOT real traders — they are fabricated personas.
actor_types_analysis.wallet_owners: FABRICATED — The 3 'users' whose wallets are analyzed do not exist. Their trading patterns, PnL, and persona data are entirely invented in cache JSON files.
actor_types_analysis.snapshotters: NONEXISTENT — There is no evidence any real user has ever purchased a snapshot. The PaymentButton.tsx component is a pure simulation (line 6: 'setTimeout(() => setState("done"), 1500)' — just CSS animation, no blockchain transaction).
actor_types_analysis.coachers: NONEXISTENT — The $4.99/mo coaching subscription is mentioned in PRD/README but has zero implementation in code. No subscription mechanism, no content delivery, no backend.

13.1.bottom_line: The leaderboard data proves real traders EXIST as an actor class. But the 3 demo wallet owners are fictional — their addresses share fabricated substrings and have no on-chain presence. Snapshotters and coachers are aspirational only. The product has proven the existence of ONE actor type (leaderboard traders) but fabricated the other three.

13.2.title: Cold-start user #2 — first non-team user

findings.team_user_assumption: The only 'user' in the system is the demo flow triggered by LOAD DEMO button, which populates the 3 fabricated wallet addresses. There is no authentication, no user registration, no session persistence, and no way for a real user to onboard.

okx_ai_marketplace_claim.stated_in_readme: README.md line 59: 'Alter Ego is listed as an agent on the OKX.AI marketplace.'
okx_ai_marketplace_claim.stated_in_prd: PRD line 455: OKX.AI Marketplace ASP listing status = 'Pending'. PRD line 428: ASP listing artifact = URL required.
okx_ai_marketplace_claim.actual_status: The PRD itself in section 9 (Dependencies) shows ASP registration as 'Pending'. The seed script (scripts/seed-demo.ts) does NOT exist in the repository — the cache files were manually created. No ASP listing URL is present anywhere in the codebase. The marketplace claim in README is aspirational/premature.
evidence_of_non_listing: No ASP listing URL found in any file.
No ERC-8004 identity token on X Layer explorer (PRD line 420 references it but no address is provided).
PRD risk #1 (line 360): 'ASP review takes >24h, misses deadline — CRITICAL risk. Mitigation: Submit ASP TODAY (July 15).' This confirms listing was NOT achieved at PRD time.

user_incentive_when_empty.analysis: The product's value proposition requires network effects: users get value from seeing their patterns compared to crowd data. But when marketplace is empty (no other users), the only comparison is against the leaderboard — which Zerion/Nansen/Debank already provide for free.
user_incentive_when_empty.incentive_gap: A new user pastes their wallet and gets: (a) pattern analysis — valuable once, (b) persona generation — entertainment value once, (c) roast battle between their own chains — entertainment value once, (d) crowd comparison — relies on leaderboard data that's publicly available elsewhere. There is NO recurring value loop and NO reason for user #2 to join when user #1 got the same value without network effects.
user_incentive_when_empty.no_referral_or_viral_mechanism_in_code: The roast battle is described as 'designed for virality' but there is zero share-to-X implementation in code. No screenshot export, no tweet intent link, no referral code, no invite mechanism.

13.2.bottom_line: There is no non-team user. The OKX.AI marketplace listing is aspirational (marked 'Pending' in PRD dependencies). No onboarding flow exists. User #2's incentive to join an empty marketplace is absent — the product provides one-shot entertainment value with no network-effect payoff.

13.3.title: Two-sided-market liquidity check

supply_side_users.description: Users who analyze wallets and generate snapshot content
evidence: src/app/page.tsx line 15: `launchDemo()` function hardcodes fake addresses: `{ address: '0xDemo...', chains: ['ethereum'] }, { address: 'SolDemo...', chains: ['solana'] }`

src/app/api/analyze/route.ts lines 11-13: The POST handler checks `DEMO_MODE === 'true' || cacheExists()` and ALWAYS returns pre-cached data. The live OnchainOS code path is unreachable in the current deployment.
No user authentication flow exists. No wallet connection (OKX Wallet, MetaMask, Phantom). Addresses are manually typed into a textarea.

demand_side_buyers.description: Buyers who purchase snapshots via x402 micropayments
evidence: src/components/PaymentButton.tsx lines 5-6: Payment is a CSS animation: `setTimeout(() => setState('done'), 1500)`. No wallet connection, no USDC transfer, no blockchain interaction.
PRD line 20: x402 Payment Settlement explicitly marked '[MOCK]' — 'Shows Simulate Payment button, no real USDC settlement.'
No x402 contract address, no Base USDC integration, no payment confirmation endpoint exists in the codebase.
README line 63 states '$0.99 via x402 to lock a permanent, shareable proof' — but the PaymentButton labels state 'Processing x402...' then '✓ Payment Simulated', openly acknowledging simulation.
No marketplace listing, no discovery mechanism, no snapshot catalog, no buyer browsing.
The PRD describes a 'Snapshot ($0.99)' product but there is no code for generating, storing, or listing snapshots for purchase.
The 'ATTESTATION VERIFIED' badge is a static pre-computed hash: `0x7f3a...b91e` (page.tsx line 118) — not a real TEE attestation.

13.3.bottom_line: Both sides of the two-sided marketplace are simulated. Users never generate real snapshots; buyers never pay real USDC. The x402 integration is explicitly labeled [MOCK] in the PRD. The marketplace listing on OKX.AI is aspirational. This is a single-player demo, not a functioning marketplace.

13.4.title: Chicken-egg resolution — cold-start mechanism

evidence: No seed script found: The PRD (lines 389-395) specifies `scripts/seed-demo.ts` must create all cache files, but the `scripts/` directory does not exist.
Cache files are manually authored JSON — not generated from real data. The wallets, trades, patterns, personas, roast lines, and comparison are all hand-written.
No user acquisition code: No invite system, no referral rewards, no airdrop, no token incentives, no social sharing implementation, no embed/widget for other sites.
No content seeding: No pre-populated snapshots, no featured personas, no leaderboard integration beyond static cache.

bootstrap_in_pitch.description: What the PRD/README claim about cold-start
claims: README line 59: 'Alter Ego is listed as an agent on the OKX.AI marketplace' — implies marketplace discovery drives users.
PRD line 46: 'x402 micropayments: Snapshot ($0.99), Coach ($4.99/mo), Battle ($1.99). Listed on OKX.AI marketplace with real pricing.'
PRD line 48: 'Roast battle format is designed for virality. Your ETH self vs your SOL self is instantly shareable.'
README line 21: 'produces a cryptographic snapshot you can share'
bootstrap_in_pitch.gap_analysis: All cold-start mechanisms exist only in prose. The code contains: (a) no marketplace integration, (b) no social sharing, (c) no snapshot generation, (d) no payment collection, (e) no user onboarding. The $0.99 price point is stated but never executed.

realistic_assessment.user_acquisition_path: None implemented. The only distribution channel is the Vercel demo URL (alter-ego-demo.vercel.app).
realistic_assessment.chicken_egg_status: UNRESOLVED — The product needs users to create content (snapshots) and buyers to purchase them. Neither side has a bootstrap mechanism. The demo sidesteps this entirely by pre-computing all data.
realistic_assessment.comparison_to_peers: Established platforms (Zerion, DeBank, Nansen) solved cold-start by being FREE and providing utility without network effects. Alter Ego proposes a paid model ($0.99/snapshot) from day one with no free tier and no utility without the network.

13.4.bottom_line: Cold-start is entirely unsolved. No bootstrap code exists — the `scripts/seed-demo.ts` referenced in the PRD is missing. The product proposes a paid two-sided marketplace but implements neither user acquisition, content creation, payment, nor discovery. The $0.99 price point and 'viral roast battle' are pitch-only.

13.5.title: Competitive landscape — Alter Ego's edge

core_functions_vs_competitors.alter_ego_implementation: Delegates to OnchainOS CLI (same data source as competitors). In demo mode: pre-cached static JSON.
core_functions_vs_competitors.competitors: Zerion, DeBank, Zapper, Nansen — all provide real-time portfolio tracking with richer UI, mobile apps, and multi-chain support. All are free.
core_functions_vs_competitors.edge_assessment: NONE — Alter Ego uses the same OKX/OnchainOS data pipeline with a LESS functional UI. No mobile app. No real-time updates.

core_functions_vs_competitors.alter_ego_implementation: Rule-based classifier with 12 hardcoded patterns. In demo: patterns are pre-authored in patterns.json, not computed live.
core_functions_vs_competitors.competitors: Nansen — labels wallets (Smart Money, Token Millionaire, etc.) with on-chain heuristics. DeBank — 'Whales' tab. Zerion — portfolio history. None specifically do 'pattern classification as persona,' but Nansen's wallet labeling is functionally equivalent.
core_functions_vs_competitors.edge_assessment: MARGINAL — The persona angle is novel in framing but the underlying pattern detection (hold duration, win rate, rug exposure) is standard portfolio analytics. The PRD (line 171) admits it is 'Rule-based (not ML), deterministic' — this is NOT technically differentiated from existing heuristics.

core_functions_vs_competitors.alter_ego_implementation: Pre-authored personas.json mapping pattern tags to archetypes. No LLM generation at runtime (PRD line 22 confirms roast lines are '[PRE-COMPUTED]').
core_functions_vs_competitors.competitors: No direct competitor for 'trading persona.' This is Alter Ego's most original feature. However: (a) it's entertainment, not utility, (b) it's pre-computed static data in the demo, (c) the persona engine maps patterns → archetypes deterministically — there are only 2 personas in the cache.
core_functions_vs_competitors.edge_assessment: NOVEL_BUT_SHALLOW — The concept of a trading persona is unique in framing, but the implementation is a lookup table with 2 archetypes ('The Professional', 'The Degen'). There is no evidence of a generative or adaptive persona system.

core_functions_vs_competitors.function: Roast battle (ETH self vs SOL self)
core_functions_vs_competitors.alter_ego_implementation: 8 pre-written roast lines in roast-lines.json and roast-battle.json. No LLM generation. Lines are static and identical every run.
core_functions_vs_competitors.competitors: No direct competitor. This is a genuinely original feature concept. However, it is purely entertainment — not a sustainable competitive moat. A competitor could replicate the concept with an actual LLM in days.
core_functions_vs_competitors.edge_assessment: ORIGINAL_BUT_EASY_TO_COPY — The roast battle is the most defensible unique feature, but: (a) it's pre-computed static text, not dynamic, (b) any competitor with an LLM API key can replicate it, (c) it has zero network-effect lock-in.

core_functions_vs_competitors.alter_ego_implementation: Static comparison.json comparing fabricated user stats against a fabricated 'Top Trader' address. 6-line comparison output.
core_functions_vs_competitors.competitors: Nansen — compare any wallet against smart money flows. DeBank — follow whales. Zerion — see what others hold. All provide LIVE crowd comparison with real-time data.
core_functions_vs_competitors.edge_assessment: NEGATIVE — Competitors provide real-time crowd comparison with actual wallet data. Alter Ego's comparison is static and uses a fabricated top trader address (6bZk5xN2fP8qR1cW9yA3tG7vL4mH0sD6jF8kB2nE5pX is NOT in the real leaderboard data).

claimed_moat_analysis.tee_attestation: PRD (line 19): TEE Attestation Generation marked [MOCK]. The 'ATTESTATION VERIFIED' badge is a static hex string (0x7f3a...b91e) hardcoded in page.tsx. No TEE is running. This is NOT a real moat.
claimed_moat_analysis.erc_8004_identity: PRD line 477: ERC-8004 identity creation is 'Via ASP registration' — which is marked 'Pending'. No ERC-8004 token exists on-chain.
claimed_moat_analysis.self_learning_first: PRD line 38 claims 'Self-learning comes FIRST' — but there is no machine learning, no model training, no adaptive system. The classifier is deterministic rules. The persona is a lookup table. Nothing 'learns.'
claimed_moat_analysis.multi_chain_persona_split: The ETH-self vs SOL-self framing is clever but it's a presentation layer over standard multi-chain portfolio data that Zerion/DeBank already provide.

findings.sustainable_edge_verdict: Alter Ego's competitive edge is 100% cosmetic: the persona framing, the roast battle theater, and the glitch-core terminal UI. None of these are technically defensible. The underlying data pipeline is OnchainOS (available to any OKX ecosystem developer). The TEE attestation is mocked. The 'self-learning' claim is misleading. With no user base, no proprietary data, and no technical moat, Alter Ego has zero sustainable competitive advantage.

13.5.bottom_line: Alter Ego's edge is presentation-layer novelty, not technical differentiation. Zerion/Debank/Nansen provide the same (or better) wallet analytics for free with real-time data. The persona/roast framing is original but trivial to replicate. No technical moat, no network effects, no proprietary data.

overall_assessment.summary: Alter Ego is a well-designed hackathon demo with strong theatrical UX, but as a product it fails every traction and grounding test. The 3 demo wallets are fabricated addresses with overlapping substrings indicating manual construction. The two-sided marketplace (users + snapshot buyers) is 100% simulated — x402 payment is a CSS animation, TEE attestation is a static hex string, and the OKX.AI marketplace listing is aspirational. Cold-start is entirely unsolved with no bootstrap mechanism in code. The competitive edge is cosmetic framing over commodity data — Zerion/Debank/Nansen provide equivalent analytics for free. The roast battle concept is genuinely original but exists as 8 static lines of pre-written text, not a dynamic system. The leadership data from OnchainOS IS real, but it's used to compare against fabricated user wallets, undermining the product's core value proposition of truthful self-knowledge.
overall_assessment.strongest_element: The roast battle as a theatrical demo concept — genuinely novel in the crypto analytics space.
overall_assessment.weakest_element: The demo wallet addresses share fabricated substrings (Wallet A and C both contain 'd45Ef8369a1b2C3D'), proving the core 'users' are fictional even within the demo.
fatal_risks: No path from demo to real users — no onboarding, no auth, no wallet connection, no real data ingestion.
Both sides of the marketplace are simulated with no plan for transition to real transactions.
The 'TEE-bound agent' claim is misleading — TEE attestation is a hardcoded string with no TEE infrastructure.
The competitive landscape is dominated by free, polished alternatives (Zerion, DeBank, Nansen) with network effects.
scripts/seed-demo.ts (the only documented path to real data) does not exist in the repository.
